messages:
anya: FYI — tenant-17 DB restore is hung at 67% during decrypt step. KMS DecryptTimeout in logs. Opened INC-4721.
chris: Can you paste the KMS error snippet and which key is used?
anya: sure — log: ```2026-03-20T22:11:03Z ERROR restore: decrypt failed key=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01 request_id=0a1b2c3d DecryptTimeout```
rahul: Was there any RBAC change to the backup-uploader / restore service accounts last night?
anya: We rolled a small RBAC cleanup at 21:50 — removed a stale iam binding from `backup-uploader-prod`. Not supposed to affect KMS grants but calling it out.
sam: @rahul can you check if the restore service account still has the ephemeral KMS grant? We use ephemeral grants for restores (ttl 5m). If the grant expired before the replay it would fail with timeouts sometimes.
rahul: Checking CloudTrail... searching for Decrypt/CreateGrant events for that key. Give me a min.
enc-bot: Audit alert: Policy change detected for role `backup-uploader-prod` at 2026-03-20T21:50:12Z by chrism.
chris: That was me — I removed a leftover binding for a jetstream user. I didn't touch CMK grants.
rahul: CloudTrail shows a CreateGrant at 2026-03-20T21:52:01Z for the restore SA, grantId=gr-0a9b8c, TTL=300s. Latest Decrypt attempts at 22:11:02Z are after the grant expired. Looks like restore job retried much later and the ephemeral grant had expired.
anya: That matches. But why did the restore retry so late? The restore worker should refresh grants before heavy IO.
sam: Two things to triage: 1) why restore was paused (saw transient DB lock in the preceding step), 2) make restore resilient to grant expiry (refresh path). Short-term mitigation: re-create a one-off grant with longer TTL and resume restore.
chris: I can create an ad-hoc grant: `aws kms create-grant --key-id abcd-ef01 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456:role/restore-sa --operations Decrypt --name resume-restore --constraints JSON` and set `--retiring-principal` if needed. Set TTL manually via our grant-ttl wrapper.
rahul: I'll run the grant creation and then resume the job. Also adding CloudTrail filter to detect Decrypt requests that return Timeout/Throttling so we can alert earlier.
anya: Thanks. After grant re-creation, restore progressed to 99% then failed on a different step (index apply). We'll track that in INC-4721.
sam: Postmortem items: - avoid ephemeral grant TTL smaller than max expected restore time for big tenants - add a preflight grant-refresh right before the heavy decrypt step - log grantId in restore runs and ship to logs - add an audit rule that flags replays > 10m after grant creation
chris: Also consider fallback policy: if decrypt fails with DecryptTimeout, try to re-request grant once (with jitter) before failing.
rahul: For compliance/audit: recording the ad-hoc grant creation and authorizing it through our change-window process. I'll attach the CloudTrail events and the `aws kms create-grant` command output to INC-4721.
anya: One more ask — can eng-sre check KMS regional quota/latency? DecryptTimeout might also be transient KMS SLA hiccup.
sam: Filing follow-up ticket SRE-1312 to correlate KMS latency, network EGW logs around 22:10-22:20.
enc-bot: Reminders — flagged INC-4721 as security-impacting and added `encops` label.
chris: Thanks everyone. I'll spin a short runbook blurb for on-call: how to create temporary grant + resume restore + verify CloudTrail. Put it in confluence under EncryptOps > Runbooks.
anya: copying that runbook snippet now into the ticket and tagging customers. Closing loop once SRE-1312 and the code fix for preflight refresh are PR'd. :thumbsup:
